oindent The quadrature law $g^2=g_N^2+a_0g_N$, i.e.\ $
u(y)=\sqrt{1+1/y}$ with $y=g_N/a_0$ (Milgrom 1999, eq.~9), has a slow strong-field tail, $

59987a58e31a049c.claim: \section{The turn-off} We keep the law where it is measured and switch the tail off above $y_t$: \begin{equation} \nu_{\rm fix}(y)=1+\frac{\sqrt{1+1/y}-1}{1+(y/y_t)^k},\qquad k=2\ \text{(default)} .
59987a58e31a049c.note: Definition, as coded in p35 (k=2 default).

21ca74ed8f834ecc.claim: \end{equation} Below $y_t$ this is the law (deep limit, landmark triplet and sum rule unchanged); above it $\nu-1\simeq y_t^k/(2y^{1+k})$.
21ca74ed8f834ecc.note: Asymptotic form is trivial algebra, but no committed output checks that the 'landmark triplet and sum rule' are unchanged. Below y_t the kernel is changed by the factor 1/(1+(y/y_t)^2), so it is not exactly the law. p49's orbital sum rule is finite only WITH the turn-off (for the exact kernel the boundary term grows), so the sum rule is changed, not untouched. Looked in p35/p36/p49 outputs.

sources.value: the sum rule needs the turn-off
